AC-0058 — web view: game rendered to ~2/3 of the screen

Root cause

At boot, the engine's C++ DisplayServerWeb constructor calls godot_js_display_setup_canvas(1280, 720) — for canvas_resize_policy=2 (the preset's "Adaptive") that branch does not set a CSS size, so the <canvas> element keeps its intrinsic drawing-buffer size (1280×720, the project viewport from godot/project.godot:19-20). The window then boots at 1280×720: a 1920×1080 page shows a 1280×720 letterboxed box anchored top-left (2/3 of 1920×1080 — exactly the reported symptom). The per-frame poll (DisplayServerWeb::check_size_force_redraw in platform/web/display_server_web.cpp:66-76, called from web_main.cpp:86) only re-syncs when the canvas changes size — and nothing in the exported JS ever forces that on load, so the 1280×720 window persists for the whole session. Any subsequent window resize did work (canvas tracks window → JS updateSize() resizes buffer → next main-loop tick re-syncs the C++ window), which is why the 1366×768 shots are byte-identical before/after the fix: only the initial-load canvas size was stuck.

Fix (Godot-side, reproducible through every build)

godot/export_presets.cfg:30 — set html/head_include (the exporter's official $GODOT_HEAD_INCLUDE injection point; content is concatenated verbatim into the generated web/index.html, so build_web.sh needed no changes):

<style>html,body{width:100%;height:100%}#canvas{width:100vw;height:100vh}</style>
<script>DOMContentLoaded → MutationObserver on #canvas width attribute
  → after 2× requestAnimationFrame (post engine-setup) kick: c.width -= 2</script>

The injected CSS makes the canvas fill the viewport at document load (buffer already equals viewport, so aspect is correct), and the one-time 2px width kick guarantees the per-frame check sees a size change right after setup_canvas, forcing the C++ window to re-sync to the true canvas size. The engine's own JS then keeps the canvas + buffer + C++ window in sync on every later resize (that path was already correct). Input mapping is handled by the engine JS via getBoundingClientRect + canvas.width/rect.width scaling (GodotInput.computePosition), so CSS scaling can't offset the mouse — verified by drag below.

Black-pixel fraction of the full frame at 1920×1080 load: ≈48% (before) → 0.0008 (after) (remainder = hotbar slots). At 1366×768: 0.0005.

Input after fix

1080p: pointer down at (960,540), 12-step drag +288px/−96px → screenshot frame change 0.473 (camera look tracked the drag, no offset). One pageerror observed is "A user gesture is required to request Pointer Lock" — headless-only artifact (no real user-gesture in headless Chromium; pointer-lock is untestable there); excluded, documented. No console errors, no script errors.
